name: RDRS Termination Method Atlas
description: Enumerates 76 method families with total classification into barrier, escape and licensed statuses. Twelve semantic rows and fourteen algebraic rows close with exact mechanisms.

program.name: The Termination Axis
program.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

oneLine: The 76-method universe is fully classified into barrier, escape and licensed statuses with closed algebraic, path-order, semantic and coverage layers.
summary: The theory fixes a universe of 76 termination-method families with a nine-valued status assignment and asks which families admit direct payload-sensitive orientation and which escape by projection, construction, transformation or nonconservative change. It builds abstract one-step interfaces with orientation predicates, semantic measures with directness evidence, and static projection transactions with seed-collapse and counter factoring. It closes the 14-row algebraic-interpretation inventory with eight mechanisms and named hypotheses for five conditional rows, the 12-row path-order inventory with KBO barriers and imported-precedence escapes, and the 12-row semantic-structural inventory with depth-barrier support. It audits the full universe with six-way and five-way ledgers and with a 16 theorem-backed plus 60 curated evidence split that is later lifted to native evidence for all 76 rows. It proves that lens-pump violations refute orientation, that payload erasure makes every orienting measure counter-dominated with no decisively payload-sensitive measure, and that well-founded lenses rule out infinite chains while bare transactions do not. Results hold under explicit hypotheses such as Big-O bounds, pump witnesses, precedence and filter data, typing non-duplication conditions, and caller-supplied factor maps for retained-coordinate factoring.
boundary: Direct payload-sensitive orientation holds on the escape side through projection transactions that transport a well-founded projected orientation back through a commuting projection with seed-collapse and counter factoring, and it fails on the barrier side where lens-pump witnesses, KBO variable-count obstructions and duplication gaps refute orientation. The obstruction is a single triple where the strict order fails, a pump violation, or a payload-erasure that forces every orienting measure to be counter-dominated. The location is recorded by the universe closure and ledger closures that place 28 families in payload-sensitive blocked, 8 in projection escape and the remainder in construction, transform and not-direct buckets, with W0 witnesses boundary-blocked and W2 witnesses admissible.

conclusions.statement: RDRSUniverseClosed holds, aggregating the 76-row count, duplicate-freeness, completeness, status totality and eight layer markers with no new mathematics.
With no hypotheses, NativeCoverageEvidenceLedgerClosed holds, so every one of the 76 rows has method-native evidence while the historical 16/60 adapter split is preserved.

With no hypotheses, CoverageEvidenceLedgerClosed holds, so the 76-row ledger splits into 16 theorem-backed rows with constructor-closed evidence and inhabited claims and 60 curated rows with no interpretation and no claim.
With no hypotheses, CoverageLedgerClosed holds, so the six-way classification is total over the 76 families with bucket counts 28, 8, 7, 13, 20 and 0 and the temporaryUnclassified bucket empty.
The 14-row algebraic-interpretation lane is closed with barrier, conditional-barrier and escape statuses, eight mechanisms and named hypothesis carriers for the five conditional rows.
The finite path-order classification is closed, covering twelve rows with KBO barriers blocked and conditional escapes under imported precedence or safe-argument hypotheses.
The twelve-row semantic-structural atlas is closed with length, duplicate-freeness, completeness, status match, terminality, mechanism totality and depth-barrier support.
The conditional and typed layer satisfies the packed closure certificate with aligned mechanisms, terminal statuses and explicit typing-barrier hypotheses.

For every StandardKBO K, StandardKBORecSuccObstruction K holds, so no finite standard KBO orients the KO7 duplicating recursor-successor root rule with schema terms tied to an actual Step.R_rec_succ instance.
For every family f, under the hypothesis that (curatedReason? f).isSome equals true, RowClaim f (u6ClassOf f) does not hold.
Given a bottleneck BB, kappa_boundary of its W0 witness equals false and kappa_boundary of its W2 witness equals true.
For every step R with payload erasure E and every semantic measure data M, PayloadSensitiveDecisive R M does not hold, with every orienting measure counter-dominated.
For every lens L, under hypothesis hBad that HasPumpViolation L holds, Orients R mu ltA does not hold.
Given a well-founded lens L, hypothesis hOrients that Orients holds, and any function f with hypothesis hf that StepChain R f holds, False follows, so no infinite chain exists.

It is not the case that for all transactions P and hypotheses SH there exists a uniform factor map from Nat factoring the retained coordinate through the counter, so the factor premise cannot be removed.

openPoints: Five algebraic conditional rows carry named hypothesis structures with monotone Big-O bound, degree bound plus pump witness, strict index below arity, argument-filter flag, and precedence plus coefficient bound, orienting toward escape under those hypotheses.
Three typing-barrier rows carry explicit non-duplication, linearity and ramification hypotheses, while non-typing rows carry no hypothesis.

Head-precedence, RPO-permutation and POP-star safe-argument escapes require imported precedence, compatibility or separation hypotheses, and the Cichon slow-growing principle is recorded as non-universal.

Projection-transaction escape requires a well-founded projected relation with projected orientation plus seed-collapse factoring and counter factoring; data-alone transactions and bare erasure are insufficient, and retained-coordinate factoring requires a caller-supplied factor map.

Classifier totality and zero-residual claims hold inside closed grammars such as the five-shape raw grammar, normalized certificates and the sixteen-row semantic ledger, and do not extend to arbitrary raw Lean functions or arbitrary Lean normalization.

Single-step orientation transport does not imply strong normalization, confluence or full dependency-pair soundness, and shim files record supersession lists with length and duplicate-freeness and introduce no axioms.

subTopics.name: direct measures, certificates and semantic classification

files.summary: Fixes the 14-row algebraic-interpretation inventory with length, duplicate-freeness and membership completeness. Assigns each row a barrier, conditional-barrier or escape status matching the universe and one of eight positive mechanisms. Introduces explicit hypothesis structures for the five conditional rows and proves a closure marker bundling inventory, status, mechanism and hypotheses.
files.conclusion: The 14-row algebraic-interpretation layer is closed with exact statuses, mechanisms and conditional hypotheses.

files.summary: The file is a compatibility shim for the historical archimedean-projection barrier name. It defines a two-entry supersession list pointing to the algebraic-interpretation and semantic-structural atlases. It proves the list has length two without duplicates and introduces no axioms or placeholders.
files.conclusion: The historical archimedean-projection file is superseded by the two named atlases.

files.summary: The file defines three witness layers W0, W1 and W2 with distinct Nat truth-level and Bool boundary-admissibility orderings. It defines layered witnesses with direct, abstract construction and projection-transaction cases plus per-layer admissibility lemmas. It packages a W0 and W2 premise into a bottleneck structure, proves W0 blocked with W2 admissible, and separates boundary-relative acceptance from truth-level existence.
files.conclusion: Under a W0 and W2 premise the W0 witness is boundary-blocked while the W2 witness succeeds, with truth-level distinct from boundary-level.

files.summary: The file closes the 13 conditional, constrained, higher-order and type-based rows with length, nodup, completeness and terminal statuses. It defines local row, mechanism and typing-hypothesis enums with atlas projection and per-row status, mechanism and hypothesis pins. It proves non-typing rows carry no hypothesis, typing rows carry one, with mechanism-status alignment, packed into a layer-closed marker.
files.conclusion: The 13-row conditional and typed lane is closed with aligned mechanisms, terminal statuses and explicit typing-barrier hypotheses.

files.summary: This file adds the semantic layer over the 76-row status ledger, defining a finite standard KBO, its weight and precedence order, and proving no such KBO orients the KO7 duplicating rule. It defines the exact DP subterm certificate and the finite usable-rules root closure with its least fixed point and projection descent. It then defines RowClaim, closed MethodInterpretation carriers, curated reasons and the total 16 theorem-backed versus 60 curated disposition, closing both the legacy evidence ledger and the full 76-row native ledger.
files.conclusion: The 76-row ledger is closed with 16 theorem-backed rows carrying exact carrier propositions, 60 curated legacy rows carrying provably no claim, and all 76 rows carrying native method evidence.

files.summary: This file is the status audit ledger assigning each of the 76 termination-method families a ten-column record with constructor, certificate, lens, seed-collapse, projection, coordinate, six-way class and Lean identifier. It defines the U6Classification refinement and proves the bucket counts partition the universe with the temporaryUnclassified bucket empty. It closes the ledger with CoverageLedgerClosed and its inhabitant rdrs_coverage_ledger_closed.
files.conclusion: The six-way classification is total over the 76 families with counts 28, 8, 7, 13, 20 and 0 partitioning the universe and every ledger row agreeing with its classifier.

files.summary: The file defines a five-way coverage classification for the 76-family RDRS termination-method universe and a ledger row recording family, Lean module, theorem identifier, classification, and friction note. It defines the master lookup coverageClassOf with module, theorem, and friction maps, plus the full row list and five filtered family lists. It proves by decide that the counts are 21 blocked, 8 projection-escape, 15 construction-escape, 20 not-direct, and 12 needs-proof, totaling 76, with every family classified. It packages these facts in CoverageSeedClosed and proves the seed-closed theorem.
files.conclusion: The 76-family universe is fully classified with proved counts 21, 8, 15, 20, and 12 and a closed seed certificate.

files.summary: Defines a 16-row DP-processor inventory split into seven projection, three inheritance and five neutral rows plus a usable-rules boundary. Characterizes projection as closing by erasing the duplicated slot, inheritance as requiring a duplication-tolerant base order, and neutral rows as needing projection pairing. Matches local statuses to universe statuses, bounds usable-rules elimination to projection pairing, and packages a closed classification certificate.
files.conclusion: The 16-row DP-processor classification is closed with projection and inheritance exactness and projection-only usable-rules elimination.

files.summary: The file defines an abstract one-step interface RDRSStep with left and right sides, an orientation predicate Orients, a descent lens with projected order and nonincrease clause, and a pump-violation existence predicate. It proves that a lens together with an exhibited violation implies negation of orientation. It records an audit anchor string for that local-contradiction theorem.
files.conclusion: A single descent-lens pump violation implies the step relation is not oriented.

files.summary: The file adds a well-founded strict codomain order to the descent lens and proves that a well-founded lens makes the reverse projected relation well founded. It proves no well-founded relation admits an infinite descending sequence and hence no infinite chain exists for an oriented step relation with such a lens. It constructs natStep and increasingLens on the reverse natural order with orientation and an infinite identity chain, proving the reverse order not well founded. It packages these as an exact counterexample to deleting the well-foundedness field.
files.conclusion: A well-founded lens rules out infinite oriented chains, and deleting well-foundedness makes that global claim false.

files.summary: The file defines the fourteen-family formalized direct-barrier grammar, seven named escape mechanisms, and a 21-method universe with classifiers for family, reason, scope, and scope witnesses. It proves unconditionally that inside holds exactly with a grammar family, escape holds exactly with a reason, the two exclude and exhaust, and families lie in the fourteen-list. It proves escape totality and that the four scope-violation escapes violate their InScope sentinels, with witnesses that both sides are nonempty.
files.conclusion: Every method is either inside the fourteen-family grammar or escapes by a named mechanism, exclusively and exhaustively, with scope-violation escapes provably out of scope.

files.summary: The file presents the free-recursor successor rule as an RDRS step and proves its instances are exactly successor-counter root steps. It defines an erasure replacing step arguments by zero and proves it is a payload erasure. It deduces that erased measures orient, every orienting measure is counter-dominated, and no semantic or certified direct measure is decisively payload-sensitive. It exhibits a counter-plus-payload weight that orients, reads the payload, and is counter-dominated.
files.conclusion: No semantic or certified direct measure is decisively payload-sensitive on the successor rule and every orienting measure is counter-dominated, even one that reads the payload.

files.summary: The file defines closed-code mechanical measures, five forbidden routes, route environments with discriminators, single-route variation, and nondependence with inhabited variations. It proves mechanical evaluation independent of each route and all routes together, with a route-sensitive control showing dependence is possible. It bridges each mechanical measure to a semantic certificate preserving the measure, proves every reflected evaluator payload-monotone, and exhibits a non-monotone semantic measure outside the mechanical image, with the counter projection as an orienting counter-dominated witness.
files.conclusion: Every mechanical measure is route-independent and payload-monotone, yet a non-monotone semantic measure with the same nondependence proofs lies outside the mechanical image.

files.summary: The file pairs raw direct-measure syntax with a normalized certificate of strict descent or abstain, plus deterministic normalization and a decidable syntactic payloadSensitive? test. It proves normalization total, soundness and completeness of the test against containsPayloadOccur, abstain behavior at both levels, and a raw-level biconditional for strict payload-containing certificates. It includes payload-only and counter-only smoke pins and imports no semantic substrate.
files.conclusion: Normalization is total and payloadSensitive? holds exactly for strict-descent certificates whose measure contains a payload occurrence.

files.summary: The file defines a six-label output and a deterministic input with certificate, optional projection-transaction evidence, and construction and transform flags. It defines a priority classifier favoring projection evidence, then construction, transform, payload-sensitive blocked, and NotDirect. It proves soundness for each bucket, zero residual for the temporary label, totality into five classes, lifting of projected orientation for projection escapes, and conditional-only retained-coordinate factorisation.
files.conclusion: Every input lands in five formal classes with TEMPORARY_UNCLASSIFIED excluded and projection escapes lifting orientation, while retained-coordinate factorisation stays conditional on an explicit factor hypothesis.

files.summary: The file defines a 20-row ledger for typed, computability, and resource-typing rows with projections to atlas families, terminal statuses, and local reasons. It proves the ledger complete, duplicate-free, of length 20, with per-row status and reason pins and typed-projection reasons. It proves simple first-order typing still leaves the direct additive barrier unoriented. It packs ledger integrity, outside-scope computability, the higher-order catalog, and typing-layer reasons into a closed certificate.
files.conclusion: The 20-row type and computability layer is closed with terminal statuses and simple typing preserving the direct barrier.

files.summary: The file defines a ten-row ledger for sharing, graph, quotient, inapplicability, translation, CPS, and quasi-interpretation rows with atlas projections and local reasons. It proves the ledger complete, duplicate-free, of length ten, with per-row status and reason pins. It proves a sharing counter strictly decreases under sharing and exhibits an idempotent-wrap quotient collapsing double wrap. It packs ledger integrity, sharing and quotient outside-scope facts, both witnesses, the sharing catalog, and reasons into a closed certificate.
files.conclusion: The ten-row nonconservative layer is closed with sharing and quotient outside direct scope plus counter and collapse witnesses.

files.summary: This file ships three concrete right-duplicating recursor schemas that are deliberately not KO7: textbook duplication, tagged-binary Bit1 recursor, and depth-counter recursor. Each carrier has a counted distinguished payload with one occurrence on the left and two on the right and a positive duplication gap. Each system is also realized as a semantic RDRS step with a payload-erasure witness, proving every certified semantic direct measure is blocked from decisive payload-sensitive orientation, conjoined in one unconditional theorem.
files.conclusion: Every certified semantic direct measure on each of the three named non-KO7 RDRS steps is blocked from decisive payload-sensitive orientation.

files.summary: This file closes eleven residual method names from expansion notes that lack explicit rows in the 76-row termination-method universe. It assigns each a terminal status in the existing vocabulary and provides typed substrate carriers with witnesses for signature-changing, probabilistic, union-hierarchical, and complexity-only rows. Scope sentinels and carrier incompatibilities show these rows differ structurally from the direct-barrier lane without widening the manuscript theorem.
files.conclusion: All eleven residual note-only method names receive theorem-backed terminal statuses and substrate incompatibilities in one closed certificate.

files.summary: This file is a stable import shim for the historical ordinal-scalarization boundary name. It defines the superseded-by list pointing to the path-order dichotomy and algebraic-interpretation atlas modules. It proves the list has length two and is duplicate-free, re-exporting the Cichon caveat, simple-termination order-type, and polynomial-KBO lift rows.
files.conclusion: The historical ordinal-scalarization file is a stable shim pointing to the path-order and algebraic-interpretation atlases.

files.summary: Fixes a twelve-row path-order inventory with mechanisms and universe-matching statuses. Reuses the symbolic variable-count barrier for five KBO variants and proves subterm-coefficient KBO barriers at weighted and carrier levels, showing the superseded unweighted record is unreachable. Imports positive and negative MPO precedence surfaces, states AC-RPO, permutation, POP* and Cichon conditions, and packages a layer-closed certificate.
files.conclusion: The 12-row path-order layer is closed with KBO barriers blocked and conditional escapes requiring explicit head-precedence or safe-argument hypotheses.

files.summary: This file defines a commuting syntactic payload-forgetting erasure and a projection-escape record carrying a projected orientation proof. It proves the factored lifted measure orients the source step from the commutation equations. It also proves every escape exhibits explicit projected-orientation evidence.
files.conclusion: A commuting payload-forgetting projection lifts a projected orientation to a source orientation, and every escape carries such projected evidence.

files.summary: This file supersedes plain payload forgetting with a static projection transaction of retained coordinate pi, soundness license sigma, and forgotten dimension phi with counter factorisation. It adds an escape structure requiring a well-founded projected relation and orientation, with a factorisation theorem lifting orientation pointwise. It shows data-only transactions are conditionally inhabited while escapes need positive success, plus a conditional bridge from legacy escapes.
files.conclusion: Static projection transactions lift orientation only with well-founded projected orientation plus seed-collapse and counter-factor data, with a conditional bridge from legacy erasure.

files.summary: This file defines closed-grammar syntax for raw direct measures and raw direct orders with no semantic content. It defines decidable predicates detecting payload-role occurrence mentions and strict Nat comparisons. Per-constructor smoke lemmas confirm the predicates evaluate as expected.
files.conclusion: A small closed grammar for measures and orders supports decidable syntactic checks for payload mention and strict comparison.

files.summary: This file lands the foundational unconditional boundary for step-duplicating recursive families. It defines families, orbits, and uniform-cost measures with delta, recursor and merge equations. It proves orbit mass is linear in counter depth, hence outside uniform-cost orientation, and mass-indistinguishable from circular references, with a catalog builder for downstream clusters.
files.conclusion: Every step-duplicating recursive family has linear orbit mass under any uniform-cost measure and is mass-indistinguishable from a circular reference.

files.summary: This file gives a computable classifier over owned additive syntax for direct measures on the counter-payload carrier. It defines counter, payload and constant coefficients with an evaluation function equal to its linear form. It proves counter-positive expressions orient and are counter-dominated while zero-counter expressions never orient, with payload coefficient separating blocked from blind, and total sound classification.
files.conclusion: The computable reflected classifier is total and sound, splitting additive measures into counter-dominated orienting, payload-sensitive blocked, and payload-blind non-orienting.

files.summary: This file defines static retained hypotheses with multiplicity coordinates, counter, and gauge invariance, plus non-descending and seed-collapse descent obstructions. It proves retained-coordinate factorisation through the counter only in factor-map-hypothesis form. A Boolean two-point step and identity transaction show unrestricted factorization is false, packaged as an exact sufficient-versus-false boundary.
files.conclusion: Counter factorisation holds exactly under an explicit factor map and fails unconditionally, as shown by a two-point Bool counterexample.

files.summary: This file defines search inside fixed W0 as a Nat-indexed enumeration of layered witnesses with a W0-boundedness tag condition. It gives a constant abstain witness showing bounded searches exist. It proves the boundary tag is uniformly false across budgets and invariant between budgets, compatibly with a separately exhibited admissible W2 witness.
files.conclusion: Boundary admissibility is invariant and uniformly false across all budgets of any W0-bounded search, independently of any admissible W2 witness.

files.summary: This file defines a section-retraction collapse pair and factorization of observables through its collapse map. It proves the factor is determined on the carrier by the section equation, noting injectivity needs a separate hypothesis. It gives the identity collapse and constructors from explicit factors or constant maps.
files.conclusion: Section-retraction collapse pairs support factorization with factor determined on the carrier and are inhabited by the identity.

files.summary: This file states semantic theorems over arbitrary measure functions rather than inspecting Lean source. It proves a payload-erasure dominance lemma where the erased measure is payload-independent and orienting, hence every orienting measure is counter-dominated and none is decisively payload-sensitive. It gives a classical total two-label classifier with soundness and a canonical counter-first-lex instance.
files.conclusion: On any payload-erasing step, and in particular the canonical counter-first-lex step, no arbitrary semantic measure is decisively payload-sensitive.

files.summary: This file packages semantic direct measures with orientation and payload-sensitivity evidence into three strata. Orientation pairs a measure with an orientation proof, raw-sensitive adds a payload-sensitivity witness, and decisive adds a non-counter-dominated witness. A repackaging theorem turns decisive certificates into decisive payload sensitivity.
files.conclusion: Three certificate strata package orientation with raw sensitivity and non-counter-domination, repackaged as decisive payload sensitivity.

files.summary: Defines a six-label semantic certificate class and a five-constructor normalized certificate carrying either typed descent or escape evidence or String audit notes. Defines a total classifier from normalized certificates to labels. Proves totality, zero unclassified output, and soundness: blocked cases carry a decisive lens-pump descent refuting orientation, escape cases carry projected orientation, and construction, transform and not-direct cases are structurally outside the direct branch.
files.conclusion: Every normalized semantic certificate classifies to a productive label with soundness: blocked cases do not orient and escape cases orient in the stated single-step sense.

files.summary: Defines a nine-row audit enum and its classification to productive classifier labels, with bucket extractors and decide-proved counts partitioning the nine rows as 0, 2, 3, 1, 3 and 0. Proves totality and zero TEMPORARY_UNCLASSIFIED over the row enum. Backs five rows with concrete S0, S2 and S6.5 orientation evidence and closes the table with a single audit-closed certificate.
files.conclusion: The nine-row audit is closed with the 0 plus 2 plus 3 plus 1 plus 3 plus 0 partition and zero unclassified rows.

files.summary: Defines a sixteen-row ledger combining nine counterexample rows with adjudication, lens-pump, classifier, and four hardening rows, each with directness and payload metadata. Adds a proof-bearing mirror where six projection rows store anchor-indexed hardened witnesses and a row-indexed claim system splits twelve typed rows from four curated rows. Proves sixteen-row length, bucket partition, zero unclassified, zero axiom-footprint strings, agreement with the audit, no plain-erasure escapes, and typed evidence for every projection row.
files.conclusion: The sixteen-row semantic ledger is closed with the stated 1 plus 6 plus 3 plus 1 plus 5 plus 0 partition, no unclassified rows, no plain-erasure escapes, and typed evidence for every projection row.

files.summary: Defines bare semantic measure data with carrier, strict order, well-foundedness, and measure function, plus caller-selected directness evidence with five propositions and proofs. Packages both into a certified semantic direct measure with projections and a five-part direct-constructor law. Proves the law holds by projection and exhibits a constant Nat measure to show the interface is nonempty.
files.conclusion: Every certified semantic direct measure satisfies its direct-constructor law, and such measures exist.

files.summary: Defines a semantic lens-pump witness as a triple where the strict measure order fails between right- and left-hand sides. Packages a decisive payload-sensitive certificate together with such a witness as a separate obligation. Proves that any witness contradicts universal orientation and projects that barrier to packaged descents.
files.conclusion: Any measure with a lens-pump witness does not orient its step, including the packaged decisive-descent form.

files.summary: Introduces the canonical counter-first-lex step on Nat times Nat and a closed five-shape raw grammar with total compilation to measure data. Uses grammar membership itself as structural directness evidence and defines a total raw classifier. Derives lens-pump witnesses structurally for blocked shapes, proves they do not orient, and characterizes not-direct shapes as orienting or payload-blind, closing with a grammar-closed certificate.
files.conclusion: The closed raw grammar has total classification with derived witnesses for blocked shapes refuting orientation and the stated orienting-or-blind split for not-direct shapes.

files.summary: Defines payload observables and lenses over abstract RDRS steps, with raw, counter-forgetting, counter-dominated and decisive payload-sensitivity predicates over semantic measure data. Proves that decisive payload sensitivity implies not counter-forgetting by using the orientation conjunct with the forgetting witness as a forbidden dominated alternative. Provides the counter-first-lex step on Nat times Nat with identity measure as a worked example that is raw payload-sensitive but not decisive through an explicit payload-blind orienter. Records that counter-domination constrains only the lhs and rhs images and that directness certificates live elsewhere.
files.conclusion: Decisive payload sensitivity strictly refines raw payload sensitivity, with the counter-first-lex measure raw-sensitive but not decisive.

files.summary: Defines a semantic projection transaction packaging a commuting projection with a projected step and well-founded semantic measure data, plus an escape adding projected orientation. Proves that the lifted measure orients the source step and that every commuting projection with an orienting measure yields an escape. Proves an escape exists exactly when some semantic measure orients the step and extracts sigma, seed-collapse, orientation and well-foundedness from every escape. Gives an identity-projection Nat witness for non-vacuity while stressing single-step transport is not a termination theorem.
files.conclusion: Projected orientation transports back to the source through a commuting projection, and an escape exists exactly when some well-founded semantic measure orients the step.

files.summary: Records four facts about every semantic projection escape and wires escapes into the legacy bridge through the identity seed collapse with trivial counter data. Proves retained-coordinate factorisation only under a caller-supplied factor map and recasts lifted orientation as witness transport for the dependency-pair bridge. Exhibits a canonical first-projection on the counter-first-lex step that forgets payload and factors through a payload-forgetting collapse, alongside an identity-projection control that keeps payload. Packages a canonical DP chain, hardened soundness, a W0-blocked and W2-succeeds bottleneck split, and search-budget invariance.
files.conclusion: The hardened semantic escape bundles four extractions with witness transport, realized by a payload-forgetting canonical projection and contrasted with a payload-keeping identity control.

files.summary: Defines raw semantic measures without directness discipline and the naive universal claim that no such measure orients any RDRS step. Exhibits four named countermodel pairs with explicit single-step orientation proofs for counter-first-lex, term-algebra oracle, nonlinear coupling and projection forgetting. Proves the naive universal false through the counter-first-lex model and records an adjudicated marker alias.
files.conclusion: The naive claim that no raw semantic measure orients any RDRS step is false, refuted by the counter-first-lex countermodel with three further countermodels.

files.summary: Closes twelve semantic and structural rows with mechanism tags and universe-matching statuses. Pins each row status by rfl and supports the match-bounds barrier through the existing max-depth no-orientation theorem. Packages length, duplicate-freeness, completeness, status match, terminality, mechanism totality and depth support into one closed marker.
files.conclusion: The 12-row semantic-structural layer is closed with pinned statuses and depth-barrier support.

files.summary: Packages universe families as atlas rows with named reason and surface classifications derived from terminal statuses. Defines the reason, surface and row structures with status projections and the 76-row mapped catalog. Proves exact length, nodup, family membership, per-row status and reason and surface exactness, and a closeout marker stating every family is represented and every row is classified.
files.conclusion: The 76 universe families appear exactly once as classified atlas rows with induced reason and surface, leaving no unclassified row.

files.summary: Provides a compatibility shim preserving the historical classifier import path without new mathematics. Defines the two-element successor list pointing to the certificate classifier and the termination-method atlas. Proves the successor list has length two and no duplicates.
files.conclusion: The historical classifier import resolves to the atlas and certificate-classifier modules.

files.summary: Defines a nine-constructor terminal status vocabulary and a 76-constructor method-family enum with a statusOf assignment. Provides the exact 76-row inventory with duplicate-freeness, length and completeness. Proves every row has a terminal status and no family-specific barrier, fixing the shared interface for parallel closeouts.
files.conclusion: The 76-row method universe is fixed with terminal statuses for every family.

files.summary: Defines bridge abbreviations for atlas, algebraic and semantic-structural marker signatures and a packed twelve-field universe-closed proposition. Aggregates the 76-row count, duplicate-freeness, completeness and terminality with eight layer markers into one closed theorem by named upstream assignment. Provides a string audit anchor and proves no new mathematics beyond aggregation.
files.conclusion: The 76-row universe and eight layer markers aggregate into a single closed certificate.

files.summary: Provides a compatibility shim for the historical transformation-method atlas import path. Maps semantic labeling and topos rows to the semantic-structural atlas and conditional and integer rewriting rows to the conditional-typed atlas. Defines the two-element successor list and proves its length and nodup marker without new axioms.
files.conclusion: The historical transformation atlas import resolves to the conditional-typed and semantic-structural atlases.

files.summary: Provides a compatibility shim for the historical tuple-interpretation boundary import path. Records that both strict tuple rows live as conditional barriers with named hypotheses in the algebraic-interpretation atlas. Defines the single-element successor list and proves its length and nodup marker.
files.conclusion: The historical tuple-interpretation import resolves to the algebraic-interpretation atlas.

files.summary: Ties together descent, projection-transaction, certificate, classifier, bottleneck and 76-row ledger layers into a capstone certificate. Defines the packed UniversalBarrierClosed proposition and proves it by assigning each field to its upstream theorem. Re-exports retained-coordinate factorisation in two explicit conditional forms to prevent unconditional reading. Provides anchor strings for claim-to-code indexes.
files.conclusion: The universal payload-sensitive direct-measure barrier is closed as a pure aggregator with retained factorisation kept explicitly conditional.

files.summary: Provides a compatibility shim for the historical WPO trichotomy import path. Maps head-precedence versus algebra-import trichotomy and polynomial rows to the algebraic atlas and order-type rows to the path-order dichotomy. Defines the two-element successor list and proves its length and nodup marker.
files.conclusion: The historical WPO import resolves to the algebraic-interpretation atlas and the path-order dichotomy.

files.summary: Reconciles DP-style projection escapes with static projection transactions for single-step witness transport. Defines DP escapes as projection escapes plus an opaque caller-supplied side-condition with conversions in both directions. Proves every DP escape restricts to a projection escape and that the projected measure transported through pi orients the source step. Stresses that orientation is not strong normalization and that no full processor framework is formalised.
files.conclusion: Every DP projection escape yields a source orientation via its underlying projection transaction, without implying termination.

files.summary: This file consumes the repaired recursive-family boundary surface and exposes a single closeout record with accessible theorem names. It defines a public completion package holding the phase-G catalog and closedness proof and a canonical surface from the repaired catalog. It proves the surface projects phase-G closedness, equals the record built from the completion theorem, and yields a public closeout-ready theorem.
files.conclusion: The canonical public surface witnesses an eleven-row deduplicated catalog in which every row projects to an existing theorem-backed surface.

files.summary: This file consumes the completion surface and records a public completion marker without restating substrate proofs. It defines a release audit record with the closeout surface, exactness, public-ready proof, row count, and per-row theorem-backed status. It proves projections preserve closeout, row count, and theorem-backed status and gives a public release-ready theorem.
files.conclusion: The release audit preserves the eleven-row theorem-backed closeout and exposes it as a public release-ready theorem.

files.summary: The file resolves every public name of the algebraic-interpretation atlas and adds four sanity theorems. It checks the row table, length, no-duplication, completeness, status, mechanisms and hypothesis carriers, including closure of the layer. The theorems state that the row list has length 14, that each row status is a barrier, conditional barrier or escape, and that two rows have the stated mechanism and hypothesis carriers by reflexivity.
files.conclusion: The algebraic-interpretation atlas has a row list of length 14 whose rows take barrier, conditional-barrier or escape status with the stated mechanism and hypothesis carriers.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the Archimedean projection-barrier supersession. It elaborates the supersededBy marker, the barrier shim marker, and the closed algebraic-interpretation layer. No new definitions or theorems are declared.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that the supersession marker, shim marker and closed algebraic layer are reachable without adding new content.

files.summary: This file is a reachability check for the 13-row conditional-typed atlas. It checks row and mechanism types, hypotheses, enumeration, nodup, completeness, alignment and closure. It proves five spot-checks pinning the row count, definitional-admitter statuses, typing-barrier statuses and hypotheses, CTRS and integer statuses, and closure-certificate row count.
files.conclusion: The closed 13-row conditional-typed atlas has the expected definitional, barrier, escape and import statuses with a closure certificate reaching the row count.

files.summary: The file anchors every String identifier from leanTheoremIdentifierOf with a #check against the live environment and prints axioms for evidence, matrix, polynomial and atlas capstones. It then reaches every public declaration of the evidence ledger and restates its coverage as examples. The examples certify the 16-row theorem-backed versus 60-row curated split of 76 rows, the native 76/0 closure, and exact-carrier claims for KBO, DP subterm, usable rules and promotion carriers.
files.conclusion: The 76-row evidence ledger is closed with 16 theorem-backed rows carrying exact native evidence and 60 curated rows carrying none.

files.summary: The file contains only #print axioms queries over the coverage ledger, seed, evidence ledger, native-semantic complement, exact-carrier promotion layer, live anchors and theory-expansion declarations. It reports the trusted-base closure of each capstone and states that any axiom outside {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound} marks failure. No new definitions or theorems are introduced.
files.conclusion: Every listed capstone, seed, evidence, native and anchor declaration is axiom-checked against the allowed three-axiom base.

files.summary: The file checks every public name of RDRSCoverageLedgerSeed and proves by rfl that representative rows have their stated classifications and modules. It proves the seed closure certificate gives total coverage over five classes, 21 blocked families, a 76-family partition and 76 direct-universe rows. All proofs are by rfl or by applying the seed closure lemmas.
files.conclusion: The seed ledger is closed over 76 rows with 21 blocked and total five-class coverage.

files.summary: The file reaches the DP processor classification closure and checks counts of projection-style, inheritance-style and neutral processors. It instantiates the classification on subtermCriterion, reductionPairProcessor, narrowing and usableRulesMinimality. The usable-rules cases show elimination succeeds only with projection.
files.conclusion: The DP processor layer is closed with 7 projection, 3 inheritance and 5 neutral processors, and usable-rules elimination needs projection.

files.summary: The file checks resolvability of the descent-lens and projection-syntax interfaces and inhabits the abstract step with a trivial Unit step. It proves the lens-violation theorem typechecks over that step and that both audit anchor strings equal their fully qualified theorem names by rfl. No concrete rewriting instance is analysed.
files.conclusion: The abstract lens interface is inhabited and its violation blocks orientation while anchor strings match their theorems.

files.summary: The file elaboration-checks every public type, classifier and theorem of the direct-barrier-scope module with #check. It covers grammar families, barrier families, escape reasons, scope classes and audit anchors. It proves nothing beyond resolvability.
files.conclusion: All direct-barrier-scope types, classifiers and closure theorems resolve.

files.summary: The file checks the type-computability no-barrier closure and reaches its row-status and survival lemmas. It proves the closed certificate holds, the row list has length 20, and three representative rows have typing-layer-barrier reasons. All proofs apply the atlas own closed and reason lemmas.
files.conclusion: The type-computability layer is closed over 20 rows with typing-layer barriers at the three named rows.

files.summary: The file checks the nonconservative escape layer closure and its completeness, status and witness lemmas. It proves the closed certificate holds, the row list has length 10, and three rows have their stated escape reasons. Proofs reuse the atlas closed, length and reason lemmas.
files.conclusion: The nonconservative escape layer is closed over 10 rows with the three named escape reasons.

files.summary: The file checks three non-KO7 RDRS instances, their steps, erasures, gap and strictness theorems and the unconditional non-sensitivity closure. It proves by decide that each instance has distinguishedDuplicationGap equal to 1. It instantiates the unconditional closure to show no payload-sensitive decisive measure exists for each step.
files.conclusion: The three non-KO7 instances have gap 1 and no decisive payload-sensitive direct measure.

files.summary: The file checks the notes-reconciliation closure, row counts, completeness and totality plus its module anchor. It then checks four typed substrate carriers that replace True sentinels: signature transformation, probabilistic, union and complexity-only, with their closure and witness lemmas. Every checked anchor is paired with a #print axioms query.
files.conclusion: All reconciliation and typed-carrier declarations resolve with axiom parity.

files.summary: The file checks the supersededBy marker of the ordinal scalarization boundary shim. It also checks the path-order atlas row count and the algebraic-interpretation layer closure it defers to. No theorems are proved.
files.conclusion: The shim marker and its two delegated closures resolve.

files.summary: The file imports the finite path-order classification module and checks its markers and theorem surfaces. It runs #check and a few #print axioms for atlas rows, classifications, KBO variants, subterm-coefficient hypotheses, head-precedence and MPO behavior, ACRPO and RPO-permutation cases, POP* variants, ordinal and Cichon caveats, and layer closure. It defines nothing and proves nothing itself.
files.conclusion: The file records resolvability of the path-order atlas rows, classifications, barrier and conditional-escape witnesses, and layer-closure checks.

files.summary: The file elaboration-checks every public declaration of the recursive-family boundary module. It instantiates recursive families and boundary catalogs on void fixtures and reaches the unconditional outside-boundary theorem and empty-catalog size lemma. No new theory is introduced.
files.conclusion: All recursive families are unconditionally outside the direct-measure boundary and catalog constructions resolve.

files.summary: The file imports the reflected direct-measure DSL and checks its syntax, evaluation and classification declarations. It runs #check for measure expressions, coefficients, evaluation linearity, reflected data, labels, classification, orientation and pump behavior, soundness and totality, and the DSL anchor, plus #print axioms for two payload soundness lemmas. It defines nothing and proves nothing itself.
files.conclusion: The file records resolvability of the reflected direct-measure DSL syntax, evaluation, classification and soundness declarations.

files.summary: The file pairs #check with #print axioms for every declaration of the semantic arbitrary classifier. It covers payload erasure, erased-measure orientation, counter domination, lens-pump witnesses and total sound classification. It also checks the counter-first-lex erasure instance and its classification.
files.conclusion: Every arbitrary-classifier declaration resolves with its axiom closure reported.

files.summary: The file checks the semantic certificate classes and total classifier with its soundness lemmas. It prints axioms for totality, zero unclassified rows and soundness of blocked, projection, construction, transform and not-direct cases. No new results are proved.
files.conclusion: The semantic classifier is total with zero unclassified rows and sound escape cases.

files.summary: The file checks the semantic counterexample audit rows, total classification, partition and closure. It checks row evidence for counter-first-lex, term-algebra closure, nonlinear coupling and DP projection. Axiom closures are printed for classification, counts and evidence lemmas.
files.conclusion: The counterexample audit is closed with total partitioned rows and evidenced witnesses.

files.summary: The file parity-checks all 218 public declarations of the semantic coverage ledger with paired #check and #print axioms. It covers row types, anchors, coverage rows, typed projection evidence, evidence-backed rows, counts and the sixteen-row closure. It proves every row has exclusive typed or curated evidence, the typed-curated split permutes the ledger, and the ledger has length 16 with full partition.
files.conclusion: The sixteen-row semantic ledger is closed with exclusive typed-or-curated evidence per row.

files.summary: The file checks the normalized raw syntax for direct measures, including raw shapes, compilation, orientation and lens-pump witnesses. It covers payload and constant measures, raw sensitivity, total classification with no temporary-unclassified rows and soundness of blocked versus not-direct shapes. It closes with the raw-grammar closure and anchor.
files.conclusion: All raw-syntax compilation, orientation and classification declarations resolve.

files.summary: This file is a reachability check for the projection-transaction hardening audit. It issues paired `#check` and `#print axioms` commands for eight theorems, eight concrete payload-forgetting projection declarations, two identity-projection control declarations, one legacy bridge and one anchor string. It declares no new theorems and proves no new mathematics; compilation confirms the audit module resolves.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that the eight projection-transaction theorems, the concrete payload-forgetting witness, the identity control and the legacy bridge all resolve with their axiom surfaces.

files.summary: This file is a reachability check for the semantic projection transaction module. It issues paired `#check` and `#print axioms` for the transaction and escape structures, their constructors and projections, the commuting-projection and nonemptiness lemmas, the four escape-requirement lemmas, the trivial natural-number instance and the anchor. It proves no new result beyond resolvability.
files.conclusion: The file confirms that every public declaration of the semantic projection transaction module resolves with its axiom surface.

files.summary: The file confirms reachability of the semantic-structural atlas by #check directives and eleven typed def pins. Each pin assigns a row to its terminal status and one pin conjoins length, no-duplication, completeness, universe agreement and absence of global orientation by tree depth. A separate pin records that tree depth admits no global orienting measure as support for the match-bounds depth barrier.
files.conclusion: All twelve semantic-structural rows pin to their recorded terminal statuses and tree depth admits no global orienting measure.

files.summary: This file captures the axiom surface of six shim marker theorems across WPO, ordinal, Archimedean, tuple, transformation and classifier modules. It contains only six `#print axioms` commands. It states and proves no mathematical claim itself.
files.conclusion: The file confirms the six shim marker theorems resolve for axiom-surface inspection.

files.summary: This file checks reachability of the 76-row termination-method atlas. It re-states length, no-duplicate, no-unclassified and completeness facts as reachability theorems. It also checks by `rfl` that standard and subterm-coefficient KBO rows have barrier status and that row status projects exactly to universe status. All proofs are projections of the underlying atlas theorems.
files.conclusion: The 76-row termination-method atlas is reachable with exact status projection and standard KBO rows on the barrier side.

files.summary: This file checks that the termination-method classifier namespace resolves. It contains only two `#check` commands for the supersession relation and the shim marker. It proves nothing beyond name resolvability.
files.conclusion: The file confirms the classifier supersession and shim-marker names resolve.

files.summary: This file checks reachability through the termination-method universe closeout certificate. It re-states the 76-row count, uniqueness, completeness over all families and per-family status totality as structural projections. It also checks the expected anchor string by `rfl`. All checks use kernel axioms only.
files.conclusion: The 76-row universe certificate is reachable with exact row count, uniqueness, completeness and anchor value.

files.summary: This file checks resolvability of the transformation-method atlas shim. It contains `#check` commands for the supersession relation, the shim marker and two conditional-typed atlas row facts. It proves no new claim.
files.conclusion: The file confirms the transformation atlas and conditional typed-row names resolve.

files.summary: This file checks resolvability of the tuple-interpretation boundary shim. It contains `#check` commands for the supersession relation, the shim marker and the algebraic-interpretation layer-closed theorem. It proves no new claim.
files.conclusion: The file confirms the tuple-interpretation boundary shim and algebraic layer names resolve.

files.summary: This file exercises the public surface of the universal payload-sensitive barrier capstone without proving new mathematics. It checks the closure structure, conditional retained-coordinate re-exports and anchor strings. It proves anchor equalities and capstone field equalities by `rfl` and replays the conditional factorisation shape with its required factor hypothesis. Its honesty record limits scope to the closed-grammar surface.
files.conclusion: The capstone surface is reachable with exact anchors and fields, and its retained-coordinate factorisation is explicitly conditional on a caller-supplied factor hypothesis.

files.summary: This file is a reachability check for the WPO-trichotomy shim. It checks that the shim namespace, its supersession marker and the two substitute closure markers for algebraic interpretation and path orders resolve. It states no theorem and uses only `#check` commands.
files.conclusion: The file confirms the WPO shim and its two substitute closure markers resolve.

files.summary: This file checks the TheoryExpansionCloseoutSurface public names. It issues #check queries for the surface type, canonical object, projection and exactness theorems, and readiness. Its five examples assert reachability, the eleven-row duplicate-free catalog with projections, exactness of the canonical record, and the row count. It proves no new theory.
files.conclusion: The public closeout surface and its readiness theorem resolve with an eleven-row catalog.

files.summary: This file checks the TheoryExpansionReleaseAudit public names. It issues #check queries for the audit type, canonical object, projection, row-count, theorem-backed and readiness facts. Its six examples assert reachability, preservation of the eleven-row closeout marker, the row count, theorem-backed status of all rows, and use of the canonical surface. It proves no new theory.
files.conclusion: The public release audit resolves with eleven theorem-backed rows over the canonical closeout surface.
